page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m2.xlarge is a burstable, shared-core virtual machine instance configured on KVM virtualization. It features 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running on an Intel Xeon Platinum 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 8.0 GB of memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The underlying x86_64 architecture incorporates instruction set extensions including AVX, AVX-512 (F and VNNI), and AES. Network baseline performance is rated at 1 Gbps, while local instance storage is absent, requiring external block storage for persistent data.

Benchmark evaluations indicate entry-level compute and I/O capability characterized by its shared and burstable CPU allocation model. Stress-ng returned a single-core score of 1070.48 and multi-core score of 4191.43, both placing in the bottom quartile. Geekbench results echo this pattern with a single-core score of 889.0 and multi-core score of 2603.0, alongside weak results for clang compilation (3809.0) and poor text processing throughput (968.0). Memory operations measured 30.76 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 27.25 GB/sec for writes. PassMark database operations scored 1026.09, and Redis SET throughput recorded 4.55 million operations per second.

The primary operational tradeoff of ecs.t5-c1m2.xlarge centers on CPU throttling under prolonged high-utilization demands, balanced by its lower resource cost profile. This profile makes it well-matched for non-critical services, staging environments, low-traffic web serving, lightweight background processing, and development workloads with intermittent processing requirements.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m2.xlarge is a burstable virtual machine instance built on KVM virtualization within the shared server family. It is equipped with 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz, paired with 8.0 GB of system memory. The system lacks local NVMe storage and includes a 1 Gbps network baseline. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate entry-tier performance consistent with burstable resource sharing, recording 889.0 in single-core Geekbench and 4191.43 in multi-core stress-ng tests. PassMark database tests and compression throughput place in the lower performance brackets, while Redis SET commands reach 4.55 million operations per second. The server provides a cost-efficient hardware profile for lightweight microservices, low-traffic web servers, and intermittent test or staging environments.
